🧹 Nitpick comments (1)
openshift/test/infraprovider/openshift.go (1)
`9-9`: **Prefer `apierrors.IsNotFound` for Kubernetes error checks over string matching.** Line 64 uses string matching on error messages, which is brittle and error-prone. Replace with the standard `k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/errors.IsNotFound` predicate, consistent with the pattern used throughout the codebase.
Suggested patch ```diff import ( "bytes" "context" "fmt" "os" "os/exec" - "strings" "time" configv1 "github.com/openshift/api/config/v1" operv1 "github.com/openshift/api/operator/v1" configclient "github.com/openshift/client-go/config/clientset/versioned" operatorv1client "github.com/openshift/client-go/operator/clientset/versioned" + apierrors "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/errors" metav1 "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1" @@ o.operNetwork, err = operatorClient.OperatorV1().Networks().Get(context.Background(), "cluster", metav1.GetOptions{}) if err != nil { - if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "the server could not find the requested resource") { - return fmt.Errorf("failed to retrieve network operator cluster object: %w", err) - } - o.operNetwork = nil + if apierrors.IsNotFound(err) { + o.operNetwork = nil + } else { + return fmt.Errorf("failed to retrieve network operator cluster object: %w", err) + } } ```
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. In `@openshift/test/infraprovider/openshift.go` at line 9, The code currently uses string matching on the error text (e.g., strings.Contains(err.Error(), "not found")) to detect missing Kubernetes resources; replace that logic with the canonical predicate apierrors.IsNotFound(err) from k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/errors (import it as apierrors) and remove the now-unnecessary "strings" import; update the error check wherever the string-based check appears (the err variable and the surrounding conditional in openshift.go) to use apierrors.IsNotFound(err) instead. ```
